question: Tell me about SHC
answer:
Shun Hing College (SHC), formerly Block A, is located at Jockey Club Student Village III (JCSV III) at The University of Hong Kong [1]. It houses both undergraduate and postgraduate students and aims to build an inclusive and vibrant community through exchanges, common experiences, and multicultural, globally oriented programming [1].

The college is led by Professor David S. Lee, an award-winning teacher active in ethics, fintech, leadership, law, and corporate governance [1]. Its Honor Code expresses the ethos: "Many cultures, one community of character, preparing to shape the future" [1]. Residents are encouraged to consider their engagement with one another, the Kennedy Town neighborhood, and the wider world while balancing academics and social life [1].

question: What do resident student ambassadors do?
answer:
The official term is **Residential Student Advisers (RSA)**, not "resident student ambassadors" [1]. The RSA team at Shun Hing College provides support to residents throughout their stay, including:

*   **Academic guidance** and planning
*   **Personal support** for challenges or simply someone to talk to
*   **Assistance with college resources**
*   **Organizing activities and events** to help residents connect with fellow students and build community [1]

For specific inquiries or to connect with the RSA team, you can contact Shun Hing College at shunhingcollege@hku.hk [2].

question: Where can I wash my clothes?
answer:
You can wash your clothes in the laundry rooms located on specific floors of each college in Jockey Club Student Village III (JCSV III). The laundry rooms are on 29/F of Shun Hing College and Chi Sun College, and on 26/F of Lap-Chee College and New College [2][3].

According to the FAQ, washers and dryers are equipped on these laundry floors, and you can refer to the operation manuals posted on the wall next to the smart meters for instructions on how to use them [1]. You can recharge your smartcard at the add value machine located opposite to the General Office Help Desk, with a minimum recharge of HK$10 [4].

question: What if I lose my key card?
answer:
If you lose your room key, report it immediately to the General Office and go through the key replacement procedure; an admin charge as shown in Appendix I of the Management Rules applies [3][4]. For a lost or damaged door key, the replacement charge is HK$100, and a key tag replacement is HK$30; borrowing a spare room key costs HK$20 per time [6]. Any charges paid for key replacement are non-refundable in all circumstances [3][4].

If you lose your Student Card (used for building access), report it immediately to HKU Registry for replacement [5]. If you forget your Student Card, you can still gain access by filling in a “Resident Entry Permission Record” and verifying at the Security Counter [4][5].

Note that the smartcard for laundry and air-conditioning is different from the room key and Student Card. If the smartcard is lost, report to the General Office for replacement; the admin charge applies, and any remaining value or replacement fee is non-refundable [1][2]. Replacement of a lost or damaged smartcard (without value inside) costs HK$50 [6].

question: How do I collect a parcel?
answer:
Based on the sources, here is how you can collect your parcels and mail items.

For registered mails and parcels, a collection memo will be delivered to your pigeon hole as a notification [1][2]. You can then claim these items at the Help Desk of the General Office by presenting your student card [4].

Important collection notes:
- Do not ask couriers to leave items at or outside the G/F Main Entrance, as these items will be discarded without prior notification [1][2][3].
- For bulky items or those that were not successfully delivered, a notification card from Hongkong Post will be placed in your pigeon hole; you can then claim the item at the Post Office as stated on the card [4].
- General Office hours are Mondays to Fridays, 09:00–18:00, and closed on weekends and public holidays [4].

question: How do I connect to Wi-Fi?
answer:
You can connect to two Wi-Fi networks available throughout Jockey Club Student Village III:

*   **“HKU”**: This service is for university staff and students. You must log in using your HKU Portal account [1].
*   **“WiFi.HK via HKU”**: This is a guest network for visitors that requires no login or configuration [1].

To do this, log in and navigate to **Campus Information Services => Central IT Services => Register Network Cards**. The registration takes approximately 10 minutes to take effect, and each student can register up to 5 network cards [2]. For further technical details, you may visit the Information Technology Services website at https://its.hku.hk/students/ [2].

10.2.  Hallways, walkways and stairs should be kept clear of furniture, trash and any other objects, so as not to obstruct passage and therefore escape routes during emergencies. Any items found in the hallways, walkways and stairs may be removed without prior notice.
11.
Public Properties
11.1.  Residents shall not remove any furniture, fitting, fixture or facilities provided for use in the Student Village without prior approval of the College Management.
11.2.  Residents should not deface, defile or otherwise damage any wall or any structure of any kind, or any furniture, fitting, fixture or facility provided for use in the Student Village, or install any new utility or fitting without prior approval from the College Management.  Residents who fail to comply with this clause shall be subject to fines imposed by the College Management.
12.
Visitors
12.1.  All visitors must be hosted and accompanied by a resident during the visit, and complete the registration procedures upon arrival and departure.
12.2.  The host resident should leave their Student Cards at the college security counter during the visitors’ visit, and collect the Student Cards in person when the visitors sign-out.

12.3.  Visitors shall observe the Rules and Regulations.  Any visitor who fails to comply with the Rules and Regulations is subject to blacklisting and refused entry into the Student Village.
12.4.  Visitors may visit the Student Village between 09:00 and 23:00.  No entrance of visitors is allowed after 22:30.
12.5.  Visitors who stay after 00:00 shall be regarded as staying overnight, and subject to fines and disciplinary actions by the College Management.
12.6.  Residents who invite visitors to the College shall accompany them during their visit, and shall be responsible for their conduct and any charges incurred by them.
13.
Electrical Appliances
13.1.  Only light electrical appliances intended for necessary personal care purposes may be used in the residents’ rooms and should be properly maintained.
13.2.  Without prior approval of the College Management, electrical appliances which are greater than 1 metre in length, width and height in total, refrigerators of any size, heaters, ovens or microwave ovens are not allowed to be brought into the Student Village.
13.3.  The College Management may confiscate any appliances or items which are not allowed to be brought into the Student Village, or any equipment used in such a way that may disturb or endanger others.
13.4.  Residents shall make their best effort to help save energy in the Student Village.
